BA: Green, blue and white horizontal stripes; shield bearing the silhouette of a fortified Bosnian town (mosque, churches) above the Vrbas, with a golden fleur-de-lys.
BC: Azure field on a green ground; the venerable patron of Bačka, robed in red, bearing the sword and the gospel.
BN: Red, blue and green horizontal tricolour; shield with the golden Nemanjić lion ascending fortified walls, beneath sun and crescent, the Danube and Tisa rivers, and the Serbian cross.
BZ: Yellow, blue and white horizontal tricolour; the crowned royal shield of the medieval Bosnian Kingdom, fleurs-de-lys and the silver bend, in heraldic descent from the Kotromanić dynasty.
CG: Crimson field with the golden double-headed eagle of the Nemanjić dynasty bearing the imperial monogram, historic ensign of the Petrović-Njegoš.
CM: Yellow field; on a red escutcheon, the rampant golden lion of Bulgarian heraldic continuity; black and azure stripes at the base recall the Black Sea littoral.
DA: Azure and or horizontal; on the chief, three crowned leopard heads, the historic arms of the Kingdom of Dalmatia, surmounted by the radiant sun of the Adriatic.
DJ: Sky-blue and maroon horizontal; a white seven-pointed mullet above; below, a sheaf of wheat, the grain wealth of southern Dobruja.
DR: Argent within a bordure or; Saint Blaise in bishop's vestments, holding his crozier and the model of the city, between the golden letters S and B: the banner of the Republic of Ragusa.
GV: Argent and gules horizontal; the crowned shield of the Counts of Gorizia, per bend azure with the golden lion rampant and bendy of argent and gules, heritage of the Goriška marches.
HZ: Navy field charged with the golden roundel of the Republic of Western Herzegovina, the Croatian chequy gules-argent within a laurel wreath, with the legend REPUBLIKA ZAPADNA HERCEGOVINA in capitals of gold.
HI: Gules with two crosses argent, after the banner held by the crest lion of the Kosača arms, Dukes of Saint Sava.
IS: Sky-blue and vert horizontal; on the azure shield, the golden Istrian goat with horns and hooves gules, beneath a small radiant sun: the historic arms of Istria.
KJ: Or, gules and argent horizontal, the Carinthian colours; on the central shield argent, the black Carantanian panther breathing flames gules, emblem of the Slovene principality of Carantania.
KM: Or field charged with the double-headed eagle gules displayed, medieval Serbian heraldry of Kosovo and Metohija.
KR: Argent, azure and gules horizontal, the Slovene colours drawn from the arms of Carniola; on the central shield argent, the crowned blue eagle of Carniola, its breast charged with the chequy crescent of gules and or.
KV: Plain horizontal tricolour of carmine, or and azure, banner of the Kvarner gulf, of solid stripe without charge.
LG: Vertical bands of vert, gules, argent, gules and vert; central shield of the Bulgarian Krum heritage, mural crown labelled “ЛУДОГОРИЕ” in Bulgarian Cyrillic, with the leaping Madara horseman.
LK: Official flag of Lika: a red band bearing the Croatian šahovnica at the hoist; azure field of the Velebit sky; a snow-capped massif; the grey wolf of Lika on the summit. A Croat state whose wolf and Velebit carry the Lika identity, the chequy anchoring Croat belonging.
MI: Per fess sable, argent and azure; on the argent band, the IYI rosette of Pliska, the imperial monogram of the First Bulgarian Empire, in sable on a circular cartouche.
MZ: Argent field; saltire of vert and gules interlaced; central shield argent with two lions rampant affrontés, surmounted by the sable kalpak of the Bulgarian voivodes, badged with a small or lion and pierced by a sword erect, heraldry of the haidouk liberation of the western Mizija.
PI: Gules field with the white crowned Serbian double-headed eagle bearing the Cross with four firesteels; in base, wavy bands of azure and argent, the Drina, root of the toponym Podriñe.
PM: Plain horizontal tricolour of celeste, gules and argent, pan-Slovenian banner of the trans-Mura territory, of solid stripe without charge.
PO: Gules, azure and gules horizontal; at the centre, a laurel wreath argent over two crossed swords, enclosing a crown and the cross argent on gules, Serbian banner of the Danubian plain.
PR: Vert field charged with a sixteen-rayed sun in or, Vergina style, the sun over the Pirin mountains.
PZ: Gules, vert and argent horizontal; central shield beneath a mural crown, with the green peaks of the Drina valley, an Orthodox church between the mountains, the golden bridge below and the small Serbian cross-shield in base; scroll “ПОДРИЊЕ”.
RO: Vert, gules and argent horizontal, Bulgarian-style stripe; from the hoist, a navy triangular pall charged with the Cyrillic letter Ш argent.
RS: Gules, azure and argent horizontal, Serbian pan-colours; central shield divided per bend, vert with three argent crescents (Ottoman heritage), azure with three golden fleurs-de-lys (Bosnian continuity for the Bosniaks of the Sanxak).
SI: Vert, azure and or horizontal; on the chief, the red Serbian cross with four firesteels; central shield with the stag of Srěm couchant beneath a tree, between wavy bands of argent on azure, the Sava and the Danube.
SL: Azure, argent, gules, argent, azure, five horizontal stripes; on the gules band, the marten running passant in proper colour, between the Sava and the Drava; in chief, a golden star on the azure of the heavens: the arms of Slavonia.
SP: Six horizontal stripes of or and gules alternating, pan-colours of the Šopski region.
ST: Argent and vert bipartite; on the central shield, the rampant Styrian panther in argent on a green field, the head crested with red flames; above, the imperial sun-crown, direct continuity of the historic arms of the Duchy of Styria.
SU: Serbian pan-colours, gules-azure-argent horizontal; on the central red shield, the sable boar’s head pierced by a sable arrow, the white Serbian cross with four firesteels at the base, totem of the Šumadija oak forests.
SX: Five horizontal stripes of gules and argent; from the hoist, a vert triangular pall charged with a golden radiant sun, Strandja highlands at the gates of Anatolia.
SZ: Seven horizontal stripes of or and argent; on the central shield with wavy water in chief, a stag couchant beside an oak tree, all azure-argent-vert, heraldry of the Western Sirmian plain.
TK: Gules; at the centre, the arms of insurgent Serbia (First Serbian Uprising, 1804–1813): two baroque cartouches bearing the Serbian cross with four firesteels and, on azure, the Triballian boar's head pierced by an arrow, ensigned with a crown between two crowned helms and two arms brandishing sabres, over a trophy of banners, muskets, drum and cannon.
TL: Field of kilim crimson; in the canton, the ridgeline of the Stara Planina in gold; in the upper fly, the Serbian cross with four firesteels in gold; in base, a wavy bar of slate blue fimbriated gold for the Nišava; a gold triangle in each corner, after the corner motifs of the Pirot kilim.
TR: Quartered gules and azure with sable cross overall; central shield gules, the rampant Thracian lion or; above the cross, a small sun in gold, heraldic continuity of the historic Bulgarian Trakija.
PA: Gules field radiated by a yellow Vergina-style sun; over all, the golden crowned Macedonian lion rampant, heraldic continuity of the Kruševo Republic and the medieval Macedonian crown.
VZ: Gules, sable and gules horizontal, broad sable middle band; on the sable, the golden Byzantine double-headed eagle displayed, charged on its breast with the kolovrat sun-wheel and holding sceptre and orb, Byzantino-Slavic heritage of the Vardar marches.
SO: Official flag of Soli: argent with a blue fess charged with the golden Bosnian lily (ļiļan), for the salt land of Soli around Tuzla.
VB: Official flag of Vrhbosna: per bend, azure with three golden Bosnian lilies (ļiļani) and barry of gules and argent, in heraldic descent from the medieval Kingdom of Bosnia of the Kotromanić dynasty.
BG: Official flag of Beograd: azure over gules, the white fortress of Kalemegdan above the confluence of the Sava and the Danube in argent and gules, with a golden ancient ship. Economic capital of the Confederation.
SA: Official flag of Sarajevo: on a sky-blue field, the city shield with the green peaks of the surrounding mountains above a black fortress gate and the Miļacka river in azure. Political capital of the Confederation.
ZG: Official flag of Zagreb: on an azure field, the white walled castle with three towers and a golden gate upon a green mound, accompanied by a gold star and a silver crescent. Judicial capital of the Confederation.
SF: Official flag of Sofia: on a light-blue field, the quartered city arms (the goddess of Serdica, the rotunda of St George, the lion, Mount Vitosha and the mineral springs) beneath a mural crown, with the motto Raste no ne staree (it grows but does not age). Defence and sciences capital of the Confederation.
BK: Official flag of Brčko: an azure field with an offset cross of gules, argent and vert and a golden triangle in the canton. Autonomous municipality under direct confederal jurisdiction.
MO: Official flag of Mostar: argent charged with a grey bend and the blue shield of the city, a rising sun above the arch of the Old Bridge over the Neretva. Autonomous municipality under direct confederal jurisdiction.
ZA: Gules with a chequy band of gules and argent at the hoist; three crowned lion heads argent, two and one: the arms granted to the County of Zagorje by the Counts of Ceļe (Ceļski), Counts of Zagorje, in the early 15th century, after the device of Louis I of Anjou for the Croatian lands.
ZL: Horizontal tricolour of gules, or and argent: the blood given for freedom, the gold of Zlatibor, the “golden pine”, and peace. At the centre, the arms of Zlatibor: a field of gold rising in pine tops into a chief argent charged with the Serbian cross with four firesteels in gold; over the field, the white falcon of Užice.
US: Gules, a cross throughout or between four firesteels or, their backs to the cross: the Serbian cross in the colours of the Palaiologan banner. Usora was held by King Stefan Dragutin from 1284 to 1316.
